claim: No test checks that the end-to-end site is set the way the guide's site settings say. The tests only check that each switch the seed sets is named in the guide, not that each switch the guide names is set by the seed, so a switch can drop out of the seed or be added to the guide without being set, and nothing fails. Also: No test shows that the guide's document-sharing switch actually stops a document being shared with the agent user. Only the field's value is checked, so a Frappe release that stops honouring `disable_document_sharing`, or a guide that names the wrong lever, would go unnoticed, although the DoD says a closing switch closes its door.
evidence: tests/e2e/test_site_settings.py:test_the_seeds_switches_are_fields_the_guide_names asserts that each field in seed.SITE_SETTINGS is in named(), which only shows the seed's switches are a subset of the guide's. test_the_seed_sets_the_guides_switches loops over SITE_SETTINGS only. test_every_field_the_guides_site_settings_name_exists only checks that the fields exist. Mutation: delete ("System Settings", "disable_document_sharing"): 1 or ("System Settings", "log_api_requests"): 1 from SITE_SETTINGS (tests/e2e/seed.py:442-448). All four tests in test_site_settings.py still pass, and so do test_rights.py and test_the_agent_user_has_the_guides_user_permission, because nothing reads either switch. The same happens if a later guide change adds a switch with a correct name (the way `enable_mcp` was added) without a seed entry: the site the DoD calls 'set as the guide says' is not, and the tests stay green. That is the same class of gap as the earlier `disable_mcp_server` breach. The only test that shows a switch working is test_frappes_mcp_endpoint_doesnt_answer_the_agent_users_key (tests/e2e/test_site_settings.py:67), and only for `enable_mcp`. On the pinned image (Frappe 16.56), `disable_document_sharing` works only through frappe/permissions.py:112 (ptype 'share' returns False) and frappe/desk/form/assign_to.py:124. It blocks only new shares: Administrator returns True before line 112, and DocShare rows that already exist still grant rights through frappe.share.get_shared (permissions.py:191-201). The guide does not mention either limit. test_the_seed_sets_the_guides_switches reads back the stored value and nothing more. If the switch's effect stopped, or the guide named a field that exists but does nothing, every test would still pass.
proposal: In test_site_settings.py, add a NOT_SWITCHES map for names the guide gives as alternatives rather than switches to set (`allow_purchase_invoice_creation_without_purchase_order`, `allow_purchase_invoice_creation_without_purchase_receipt`), each with its reason, like NOT_FIELDS. Then assert named() - set(NOT_FIELDS) - set(NOT_SWITCHES) == {field for _, field in SITE_SETTINGS}. Removing a seed entry, or adding a guide switch without one, then fails. Add an e2e test that, with the seed's settings, has a non-Administrator user who holds share rights on Sales Invoice call frappe.share.add for the agent user and get refused. It would also check that assigning that user's draft to the agent user is refused rather than auto-shared. Optionally, the guide could add that existing DocShare rows for the agent user (Assign To creates them while sharing is on) should be removed when the switch is turned off.

verdict.reason: I checked this by reading the test assertions, not by running anything. Under REQ-002-PRS-NF013 the DoD says "the end-to-end site is set as the guide says". The guide's site settings (docs/guides/configuration.md, Site settings) name these switches: cust_master_name, supp_master_name, disable_document_sharing, log_api_requests and enable_mcp. They also name two alternatives (allow_purchase_invoice_creation_without_purchase_order/_receipt) and two names that are not fields (outside_text, disable_mcp_server). In tests/e2e/test_site_settings.py, the test test_the_seeds_switches_are_fields_the_guide_names (line 53) only checks that each SITE_SETTINGS field is in named(), so it shows seed ⊆ guide. test_the_seed_sets_the_guides_switches (line 60) loops over SITE_SETTINGS only, and test_every_field_the_guides_site_settings_name_exists only checks that the fields exist. A grep of tests/ and harness/ finds disable_document_sharing and log_api_requests only in tests/e2e/seed.py:445-446, and no test reads either one. If either entry is deleted from SITE_SETTINGS (tests/e2e/seed.py:442-448), the seed no longer sets it. All four site-settings tests still pass, and so do test_rights.py and the user-permission test. A guide switch added without a seed entry also stays green. Only enable_mcp is guarded, by the 404 check of the MCP endpoint test at line 67. SECURITY.md:29 puts the docs in scope, and docs/backlog/backlog.md has no open item on this. A test closes the gap within the current spec: in test_site_settings.py, assert that named() minus NOT_FIELDS minus a reasoned map of alternatives equals the set of SITE_SETTINGS fields. The finding's second part asks for a test of what disable_document_sharing actually does. That part is weaker, because the DoD's 'closes it' clause speaks of a switch that closes an endpoint, and document sharing is a sharing lever rather than an endpoint. The confirmed and fixable core is the missing guide-to-seed check. None of the listed patterns fits: the seed is test code, not an argument Enterich sends to ERPNext.

claim: The guide's User Permission on the assigned company, which test_rights.py calls 'ERPNext's own barrier behind Enterich's company filter', is only shown to exist on the end-to-end site, never to refuse anything. If the guide's instruction stopped restricting the agent user's key to the assigned company, no test would notice.
evidence: The new test tests/e2e/test_rights.py:test_the_agent_user_has_the_guides_user_permission compares the User Permission rows the seed wrote (tests/e2e/seed.py:351-357) against the expected values. That checks the seed against itself. The end-to-end site has a single company (COMPANY): tests/e2e has no second company and no request by the agent key for another company's document. If the User Permission did nothing, for example because the guide's 'marked as default' row came with an applicable_for or apply_to_all_doctypes setting that leaves out the draft DocTypes, or because a Frappe bump stopped applying user permissions to token requests, every e2e test would still pass, because each one only reads the assigned company.
proposal: Seed a second company with one sales invoice and one journal entry made by Administrator. Add an e2e test in which the agent user's key (the `agent` fixture) calls frappe.client.get and frappe.client.get_list on them and gets refused or an empty list, and the same calls succeed for the assigned company.

verdict.reason: The finding holds as an unproven gap. docs/guides/configuration.md:60 tells the site to give the agent user "A User Permission on the assigned company, marked as default". REQ-001 (req-001-core.md:656) and REQ-002-PRS-NF013 (req-002-service.md:292) also require it. The only test on it is tests/e2e/test_rights.py:351-358 (test_the_agent_user_has_the_guides_user_permission). That test reads back the User Permission rows that tests/e2e/seed.py:351-357 wrote, so it checks that the row exists, not that it refuses anything. The end-to-end site has a single company (seed.py:18 COMPANY, made once at seed.py:297-307). A grep of tests/e2e finds no second company and no request by the agent key for another company's document. Every e2e use of COMPANY (test_drafts, test_ceiling, test_tax_rules, test_invoicing) reads or writes the assigned company only. If the User Permission restricted nothing, no e2e test would fail. Possible causes: different applicable_for or apply_to_all_doctypes settings that leave out the draft DocTypes, or a different way the guide's row behaves. The tests of "another company's ... answers as unknown" in tests/integration (for example test_order_to_cash.py:466, test_record_to_report.py:270, test_bank_and_cash.py:320/460, test_procure_to_pay.py:325) run against the fake ERPNext. They test Enterich's own company filter, not ERPNext's barrier, so they don't close this gap. Nothing makes it out of scope. SECURITY.md lists "The docs: a guide whose instructions leave a deployment open" and "reaching another company's data" as in scope. backlog.md does not list it, and no spec says the barrier is meant to be untested. One limit: a Frappe change in how user permissions apply is out of scope under SECURITY.md, but a gap in whether the guide's instruction works is in scope. This is not a breach. Enterich's company filter still stands in front, and nothing here was reproduced as a reached company. The fix is an e2e test inside the current specs, so the class is fix. seed.py would add a second company with an Administrator-made sales invoice and journal entry. test_rights.py would then show that the agent key's frappe.client.get and get_list on them are refused or come back empty, while the same calls on the assigned company succeed.

claim: The guide's document-sharing switch keeps drafts-only, because a share with submit gives the agent user's key submit on that document past its role. No test checks that the switch closes this: the new tests only check that `disable_document_sharing` exists as a field and that the seed sets it to 1.
evidence: The change added the seed's SITE_SETTINGS (tests/e2e/seed.py:442-461) and tests/e2e/test_site_settings.py. The DoD of REQ-002-PRS-NF013 that the change added says 'A switch that closes an endpoint closes it to the agent user's key', but only the MCP switch has such a test (test_frappes_mcp_endpoint_doesnt_answer_the_agent_users_key). For sharing, test_the_seeds_switches_are_fields_the_guide_names and test_the_seed_sets_the_guides_switches only check that the field exists and holds 1. The ceiling tests (tests/e2e/test_ceiling.py) run with no DocShare at all. In Frappe's permissions.py:112 the switch only refuses ptype 'share'. Shares that already exist still count: false_if_not_shared (permissions.py:179-211) counts 'submit' as a share right. I ran a probe on the local e2e site (v16.55.0, sharing disabled by the seed) and rolled it back. The agent user's has_permission('Sales Invoice','submit', its own draft) was False before a DocShare with submit=1 and True after it. Administrator could still call frappe.share.add with submit=1 while sharing was disabled. So a site that has a share with submit from before the switch, or one an Administrator makes after it, lets the agent's key submit, and no test would notice. Neither would a Frappe release that stops honouring the switch in frappe.share.add, or a field renamed so that it exists but no longer guards sharing.
proposal: Add an e2e test to test_site_settings.py or test_ceiling.py. With the seed's switches set, a non-Administrator desk user with share rights on Sales Invoice calls frappe.share.add for one of the agent user's drafts with submit=1, and it is refused with PermissionError. After that, the agent's key still gets a PermissionError from frappe.client.submit on that draft. Also add a test that the seed holds no DocShare for the agent user (site.get_list('DocShare', {'user': AGENT}) == []). Then add a line to the guide's sharing bullet: turning the switch off doesn't revoke shares that already exist (remove any DocShare for the agent user), and Administrator can still share.

verdict.reason:
The gap is real: no test notices if the sharing switch stops working. The guide (docs/guides/configuration.md:79) tells deployments to turn document sharing off because a user with share rights can otherwise pass the agent user more rights, such as submit, which breaks drafts-only (SECURITY.md scope: submitting a document). REQ-002-PRS-NF013's DoD (docs/specs/req-002-service.md:292) asks that each field the guide names exists, that the e2e site is set as the guide says, and that a switch that closes an endpoint closes it.

What the tests check now, in tests/e2e/test_site_settings.py:
- test_every_field_the_guides_site_settings_name_exists and test_the_seeds_switches_are_fields_the_guide_names only check that the fields exist.
- test_the_seed_sets_the_guides_switches only checks that the values match SITE_SETTINGS (tests/e2e/seed.py:442-461). It loops over SITE_SETTINGS, so dropping the entry there would not fail it either.
- Only the MCP switch has a test of what it does (test_frappes_mcp_endpoint_doesnt_answer_the_agent_users_key).

A search of tests/ for share/DocShare finds no test that runs frappe.share.add. The only hit is seed.py:377, the name 'share' in PERMISSION_TYPES, which grants no share right. The ceiling tests in tests/e2e/test_ceiling.py run with no DocShare.

On the running e2e backend (v16.55.0), the switch works only through frappe/permissions.py: has_permission returns False for ptype 'share' when disable_document_sharing is set. Its Administrator check comes first, so Administrator can still share. frappe/share.py add() has no check of its own. So a Frappe release that moves or drops that check, or a field that still exists but no longer guards sharing, would leave the guide's switch doing nothing, and no test would fail. The behaviour can be observed: a desk user with share rights on Sales Invoice calls frappe.share.add with submit=1 on the agent's draft. With the switch on it is refused; with it off it goes through and the agent key can submit.

Class fix: an e2e test in test_site_settings.py closes it under the current DoD. It needs a share-rights user (the test can create one), share.add refused with PermissionError, and the agent's frappe.client.submit on that draft still refused. A test that the seed holds no DocShare for the agent user belongs there too. The other part of the proposal is a guide line saying that turning the switch off doesn't remove shares that already exist. That changes a guide, so it is a proposal of its own. Administrator sharing is outside this, since Administrator holds every right anyway.

Not a confirmed breach: I didn't reproduce one, and a site that already holds a submit share gives the agent user more than the guide says, which SECURITY.md puts out of scope.

claim: An insert that Enterich gives up on (the operation's 60 s deadline or the 30 s call timeout), but that ERPNext still commits, is seen by no later count while it runs. Its lock is already released, so creates sent in that window in one process pass ENTERICH_MAX_DRAFTS_PER_HOUR. This breaks the new 'creates that run at the same time in one Enterich process SHALL count each other' and the guide's new bound of 'at most one create per instance besides the first'.
evidence: drafts.py:119-138 holds context.creating[doctype] from the count to `await context.erpnext.insert(...)`. When anyio.fail_after(OPERATION_TIMEOUT) in tools/__init__.py:305 or fail_after(CALL_TIMEOUT) in erpnext.py:_call cancels that await, the lock is released at once, but the POST has already gone out and ERPNext finishes and commits it (a Frappe worker doesn't stop when the client disconnects). The agent can push a create's deadline to expire during its insert without making ERPNext slow: it sends creates in parallel, the later ones wait on the per-DocType lock, and that wait comes out of their 60 s deadline (_attempt starts the deadline before op.run). Scratch test, not in the repo: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ubuntu-dev-enterich/0431a6bc-d8e6-4381-9c7d-b9072faa4363/scratchpad/limits/test_inflight.py. It uses the integration fakes and the fixtures of test_order_to_cash_drafts, with OPERATION_TIMEOUT=1.0 and limit 2. The first POST takes 1.5 s in the fake, which commits it on a timer as ERPNext would. Enterich answers that create with 'The operation took longer than 1 seconds.' Two creates sent right after both go through. Result: 3 drafts by the agent user in the hour with the limit at 2 ('limit 2 drafts 3'). Each create that counts while a given-up insert is still in flight can add one draft beyond the limit, in a single instance, which goes past the bound docs/guides/configuration.md now states. tests/integration/test_order_to_cash_drafts.py::test_creates_sent_at_once_dont_get_past_the_limit only covers inserts that answer within their time.
proposal: Test: in the integration suite, make ERPNext commit an insert after Enterich gave up on it (as in the scratch test), then send creates right away. With the limit 2, assert that at most 2 drafts exist. Fix: when an insert under the lock ends without an answer (cancelled, timed out, or ErpnextError after the request was sent), don't release the lock straight away. Either keep an in-process record per DocType of 'unconfirmed' inserts with their time, which later counts add until a count lists them or an hour has passed, or keep the lock until a re-count or a duplicate lookup shows whether the draft landed. Shield that bookkeeping from the operation's cancel scope.

verdict.reproduction: I copied the tracked files to a scratch copy (scratchpad/repo) and put the finding's scratch test there as tests/integration/test_zz_inflight.py, so it picks up the integration conftest's `limited` and `erp` fixtures. It sets tools.OPERATION_TIMEOUT to 1.0 and uses the limit DRAFTS_PER_HOUR=2. The fake holds the first Sales Invoice POST for 1.5 s and commits it on a 1.5 s timer, the way a Frappe worker finishes after the client has gone. Then it sends two creates with different quantities, so the duplicate check doesn't catch them. I ran it with `uv run --no-sync pytest tests/integration/test_zz_inflight.py -s`. Output: the first create answered 'The operation took longer than 1 seconds.', both later creates succeeded (errors [False, False]), and the fake held 'limit 2 drafts 3' by the agent user in the last hour. The test passed, which means the breach is there.
verdict.reason: src/enterich/tools/drafts.py:118-138 holds context.creating[doctype] only while `await context.erpnext.insert(...)` runs. When anyio.fail_after(OPERATION_TIMEOUT) in src/enterich/tools/__init__.py:303-305 (or the call timeout) cancels that await, the lock is released at once. The POST is already on its way, and ERPNext commits it afterwards. A count made in that window misses the draft, so in one process the creates pass ENTERICH_MAX_DRAFTS_PER_HOUR. Two texts state what should hold and are broken by this: REQ-001-PRS-F019 (docs/specs/req-001-core.md:456), which says creates at the same time in one process SHALL count each other, and docs/guides/configuration.md:46, which bounds the excess at one per instance besides the first. This is in scope: SECURITY.md:25 names the configured limit of drafts per hour. The backlog doesn't list it, and no spec says this behaviour is intended. The duplicate check (REQ-001-PRS-F005) doesn't close it, because the agent picks the inputs and can vary them. The create description's advice to list drafts after a timeout depends on the client, and AGENTS.md says no limit may depend on the client. The only test of parallel creates, test_creates_sent_at_once_dont_get_past_the_limit, has inserts that answer in time. The fix stays within the current specs: keep the given-up insert counted, either with an in-process record of unconfirmed inserts or by keeping the lock until a re-count, and shield that step from the cancel scope. The test that closes it belongs in tests/integration/test_order_to_cash_drafts.py next to the existing limit tests. It can use erp.slow and a delayed commit as the scratch test does, with no change to the fakes.

claim: If any character other than the few excluded or stripped ones follows a URL's host, the host check finds nothing, so a company's URL in Markdown bold, a table cell, a brackets pair or a shell default passes.
evidence: URL captures the authority up to one of / whitespace " ' < > ( ) ` \ ? #. _host only strips trailing . , ; : and then requires NAME.fullmatch, otherwise it returns None (treated as a placeholder). I ran offending() through `uv run python -I` with a made-up company host <company-host> (a .de name). It returned [] for each of `**https://<company-host>**`, `${URL:-https://<company-host>}`, `[https://<company-host>]`, `https://<company-host>|`, `https://<company-host>!` and `https://<company-host>_`. The same host in a plain https URL, uppercased, or followed by a dot was reported. Steps: write the deployment's URL in bold into docs/ (or into a harness/runs record, which is committed) and push. test_no_tracked_file_names_a_host_or_email_address_of_a_deployment stays green.
proposal: Test: extend test_a_deployments_host_and_email_address_are_found to plant the company host wrapped in **, }, ], |, ! and _, and expect each one reported. Fix: take the host as the longest NAME or IP prefix of the authority (re.match of a host pattern at its start) instead of a fullmatch on the whole remainder. Treat as a placeholder only an authority that starts with a template character such as { or $.

verdict.reproduction: I wrote /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ubuntu-dev-enterich/0431a6bc-d8e6-4381-9c7d-b9072faa4363/scratchpad/repro_host.py, which loads tests/repo/test_deployment_neutral.py through importlib and calls offending() on lines that hold a made-up company host (erp.acme-gmbh joined with .de, the same planted host the module's own test uses). I ran it with `uv run python -I`. A plain `https://<host>` and `| https://<host> |` were reported. offending() returned [] for `**https://<host>**`, `${URL:-https://<host>}`, `[https://<host>]`, `https://<host>|`, `https://<host>!`, `https://<host>_` and `https://<host>*`. So a deployment's URL written in Markdown bold or brackets, in a shell default, or right before a table pipe gets past test_no_tracked_file_names_a_host_or_email_address_of_a_deployment.
verdict.reason: The finding holds. In tests/repo/test_deployment_neutral.py, URL (line ~49) captures the authority up to `/`, whitespace, a quote, `<>()`, a backtick, a backslash, `?` or `#`. Characters such as `*`, `}`, `]`, `|`, `!` and `_` stay inside the capture. _host (line ~58) strips only trailing `.,;:`, then accepts the host only if NAME.fullmatch matches. Otherwise it returns None, which offending() treats as a placeholder and skips. REQ-002-PRS-NF014 (docs/specs/req-002-service.md:296) says each host in a URL SHALL be allowed, and its DoD says the check "finds each host in a URL". The promise "nothing-of-a-deployment" (AGENTS.md rule, promises.jsonl line 11) breaks for these common Markdown and shell forms. It is in scope: SECURITY.md:17 covers anything that breaks the service spec's promises, and none of the out-of-scope items applies. docs/backlog/backlog.md lists nothing about this, and the specs don't say the behaviour is intended; the module docstring says None is meant only for placeholders, templates and single labels. The fix stays in the same file, within the current specs: add planted forms to test_a_deployments_host_and_email_address_are_found, then take the host as the longest NAME or IP prefix of the authority, so templates such as `{host}` still pass. That makes it class fix. None of the listed patterns fits.

claim: A URL written escaped (JSON `https:\/\/`, or percent-encoded `https%3A%2F%2F` as in a redirect_uri) is never matched, and neither is a host given without a scheme, so a deployment's host gets in through config, JSON or YAML text.
evidence: URL requires a literal `://` right after the scheme. offending() returned [] for `https:\/\/<company-host>`, `https%3A%2F%2F<company-host>` and `ENTERICH_ERPNEXT_URL=<company-host>` (scheme left out). AGENTS.md's rule forbids hostnames in general, not only hosts inside an unescaped URL, and the harness writes JSON records into the repository (harness/runs/*), where an escaper or a URL-encoded OAuth parameter can produce these forms.
proposal: Test: plant the company host as a JSON-escaped URL, a percent-encoded URL and a bare `KEY=host` value, and expect each one found. Fix: before matching, unescape `\/` and percent-decode each line. Also check bare dotted names that end in a public suffix in the value of assignments and YAML keys (or every NAME token whose top-level domain isn't a file extension), with the same allow list.

verdict.reproduction: I wrote a throwaway test at /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ubuntu-dev-enterich/0431a6bc-d8e6-4381-9c7d-b9072faa4363/scratchpad/test_escaped.py. It imports offending() from tests/repo/test_deployment_neutral.py and plants a made-up company host (erp.acme-gmbh.de, built by joining strings) in four forms: (1) a JSON-escaped URL `{"u": "https:\/\/erp.<host>/mcp"}`, (2) a percent-encoded redirect_uri inside an allowed URL, `https://id.example.com/auth?redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Ferp.<host>%2Fcb`, (3) a bare `ENTERICH_ERPNEXT_URL=erp.<host>` with no scheme, (4) a plain `https://erp.<host>` as the control. I ran `uv run pytest -q <file>`: 3 failed, 1 passed. offending() returned [] for forms 1-3, so the host got past the check, and it found only the plain URL in form 4.
verdict.reason: The check misses a URL whose `://` is escaped. tests/repo/test_deployment_neutral.py:47 defines URL as `[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*://(...)`, which needs a literal `://`, so `https:\/\/` and `https%3A%2F%2F` never match. The URL group also stops at `\` and `?`. REQ-002-PRS-NF014 says each host in a URL SHALL be allowed. Its Definition of Done says the check finds each host in a URL and that a company's host in a URL, planted in a file, fails it. A JSON-escaped or percent-encoded URL is still a URL, so this is a breach within the current spec. It can be closed by a test in the same module plus unescaping `\/` and percent-decoding each line before matching, so the class is fix. SECURITY.md's scope does not exclude it, and docs/backlog/backlog.md does not list it. One caution on how likely it is: harness/*.py writes JSON with json.dumps, which does not escape `/`, so form 1 mainly comes from other writers. The bare scheme-less host (form 3) goes beyond the spec, which covers only a host in a URL plus email addresses. Catching bare dotted names would be a spec change (a proposal), not part of this fix.

claim: A tracked file that isn't valid UTF-8 is skipped whole, so a deployment's hosts and email addresses in a Latin-1/cp1252 text file (such as a CSV export with an umlaut) are never checked.
evidence: The loop calls path.read_text(encoding='utf-8') and `continue`s on UnicodeDecodeError, which skips the file entirely. Steps: commit a fixture or notes file saved as cp1252 that contains one byte such as 0xE4 and also a URL and email address at a company's domain. The whole-repo test passes. Only the in-memory helpers are tested; no test feeds the scan a file that fails to decode.
proposal: Test: put a non-UTF-8 text file with a company host into a temp git repo (or patch tracked()), and expect it reported. Fix: read the bytes and decode with errors='surrogateescape' (or as latin-1), skipping only files git marks as binary (`git ls-files --eol` / `git grep -I`). Alternatively fail the check on an undecodable file that isn't listed as binary.

verdict.reproduction: I made a throwaway git repo under the scratchpad (/tmp/claude-1000/-home-ubuntu-dev-enterich/0431a6bc-d8e6-4381-9c7d-b9072faa4363/scratchpad/nf014/repo) and committed two files. notes.csv is saved as cp1252 and holds 'Gräfe' (byte 0xE4) plus https://erp.<acme-gmbh.de> and buchhaltung@<acme-gmbh.de>. ok.txt is UTF-8 and holds the same URL. A scratch pytest file (test_repro.py) loads tests/repo/test_deployment_neutral.py, uses monkeypatch to point ROOT at the throwaway repo and to make tracked() return one file, then calls test_no_tracked_file_names_a_host_or_email_address_of_a_deployment(). Ran with `uv run pytest`. For ok.txt the check fails as it should (it raised AssertionError). For notes.csv it raised nothing: 'DID NOT RAISE AssertionError'. So a company's host and an email address at its domain, in a tracked text file that isn't UTF-8, pass the check.
verdict.reason: tests/repo/test_deployment_neutral.py:120-123 reads each tracked file with read_text(encoding='utf-8') and runs `continue` on UnicodeDecodeError, treating the file as binary. A Latin-1 or cp1252 text file with one non-ASCII byte is therefore never scanned. REQ-002-PRS-NF014 (docs/specs/req-002-service.md:298-304) requires 'a check over every tracked file' to find each host and email address, so this breaks the spec as written. It also breaks the nothing-of-a-deployment promise in AGENTS.md. SECURITY.md's scope covers anything that breaks the REQ-002 promises, and its out-of-scope list doesn't mention this. docs/backlog/backlog.md has no open item on it (searched for utf, encod, NF014 and binary). No spec says the skip is intended. The fix stays within the current specs: add a test in tests/repo/test_deployment_neutral.py that feeds the scan a non-UTF-8 text file holding a planted company host (patch ROOT and tracked(), as the reproduction does) and expects it reported. Then change the read to decode the bytes losslessly (latin-1 or surrogateescape) and skip only files git marks as binary, or fail on an undecodable file that git doesn't list as binary. None of the listed patterns fits.

claim: The host check reads only the working tree at the tip, so a deployment's host added in one commit and removed in a later commit of the same branch reaches main's public history through the merge commit.
evidence: tests/repo/test_deployment_neutral.py scans `git ls-files` contents as checked out, and CI runs it once (`uv run coverage run -m pytest -q`). Only gitleaks goes over every pushed commit (ci.yml 'gitleaks over the pushed commits', fetch-depth 0). main merges with merge commits (git log --merges: 'Merge pull request #83', '#82', '#43'), which keep every commit of the branch. Steps: commit 1 adds a company's URL to docs/guides, commit 2 removes it, open a PR. The check is green and the host stays in the repository after the merge. The AGENTS.md rule says nothing of a deployment goes into the repository, which includes its history.
proposal: Test: in tests/repo/test_workflows.py, assert that a CI job runs the host check over each pushed commit's added lines, for example over `git log -p base..head`. Fix: run offending() on the added lines of each commit in the pushed range, as the gitleaks step does for secrets, or squash-merge only.

verdict.reason: What the finding describes is true: tests/repo/test_deployment_neutral.py:113-121 reads only the `git ls-files` contents at the tip, and only gitleaks runs over each pushed commit. But the spec asks for exactly that split. REQ-002-PRS-NF014 (docs/specs/req-002-service.md:298-308) asks for "A check over every tracked file" for hosts and email addresses. It asks for a per-commit scan only for secrets: "Each pushed commit SHALL pass a secret scan" and "CI scans each pushed commit for secrets". The test module's docstring draws the same line: the host check covers tracked files, and credentials are gitleaks' part. The spec puts the two scopes side by side on purpose, so the tip-only host check is intended behaviour, and the task's rules refute a breach in that case. Checking the history too, or making main squash-merge only, would mean changing REQ-002-PRS-NF014 and the merge policy, not fixing a breach of the current contract. Nothing in the development guide or the ADRs sets a merge strategy. SECURITY.md's scope and docs/backlog/backlog.md don't mention this either. I ran no throwaway test: the spec point decides it, and a test would only show what the code plainly does. If the operator wants history covered, it can come back as a proposal to amend REQ-002-PRS-NF014.

claim: No test plants a public IP address, so if the IP branch were weakened to allow every address, no test would notice and a deployment's public server address would pass.
evidence: test_examples_placeholders_and_addresses_that_arent_public_pass uses only 127.0.0.1, ::1 and 10.0.0.5, which all expect an allow. test_a_public_host_passes_only_from_the_list and test_a_deployments_host_and_email_address_are_found use only names. A mutant that changes `return not address.is_global` to `return True`, or that removes the `[` IPv6 branch of _host, keeps every test green, because the tracked files currently hold no public IP.
proposal: Test: assert that offending() reports a planted global IPv4 address and a bracketed global IPv6 address in URLs. Build both from parts so that the test file itself doesn't name them.

verdict.reason: This is the place that keeps the promise. REQ-002-PRS-NF014's DoD asks the check to find "each host in a URL", and in tests/repo/test_deployment_neutral.py an IP address in a URL is a host: url_host_allowed() returns `not address.is_global` for addresses (line ~80), and _host() handles the bracketed IPv6 form. Only this module tests the check: a search of tests/ and harness/ for url_host_allowed, offending( and deployment_neutral finds no other test. I copied the module to the scratchpad with ROOT pointed at the repo and changed `return not address.is_global` to `return True`. All 4 tests still passed ("4 passed"). Two of them use names only (test_a_deployments_host_and_email_address_are_found, test_a_public_host_passes_only_from_the_list). test_examples_placeholders_and_addresses_that_arent_public_pass uses only 127.0.0.1, [::1] and 10.0.0.5, and expects all of them to be allowed. The tracked-files scan passes because no tracked file holds a public IP. So no test would notice a public IP in a URL being let through. Removing the `[` branch also goes unnoticed: a bracketed address then becomes "[2001", which is neither an address nor a name, so it is skipped. That is the same outcome the private [::1] case expects. Nothing in SECURITY.md, the backlog or the specs says this is intended. It can be closed with a test that needs no spec change: plant a global IPv4 address and a bracketed global IPv6 address in URLs, both built from parts, and assert that offending() reports each one.

claim: The whole-repo check passes vacuously if tracked() yields no files or the read is skipped, and no test notices: nothing proves the scan reaches a tracked file or names file, line and host as the DoD asks.
evidence: test_no_tracked_file_names_a_host_or_email_address_of_a_deployment only asserts found == []. The two mutants `return []` in tracked() and an except clause widened to `except Exception` both pass all four tests. The DoD's 'naming file, line and host' is formatted only inside that test, and the test never runs that formatting on a hit.
proposal: Test: run the file scan, factored into a function that takes a list of paths, on a temp file with a planted company host. Assert the message `<relative path>:<line>: <host>`. Also assert that tracked() includes a known file such as AGENTS.md.

verdict.reproduction: I copied tests/repo/test_deployment_neutral.py into the scratchpad twice, with ROOT pointed at the repo. Mutant 1 makes tracked() return []. Mutant 2 widens the except clause to `except Exception` and reads files as ascii, so every file that isn't plain ASCII gets skipped. I ran `uv run pytest` on both copies and all 8 tests passed (4 per mutant), so neither mutant is caught.
verdict.reason: The DoD of REQ-002-PRS-NF014 (docs/specs/req-002-service.md:304) asks for a check over every tracked file that fails on a disallowed host and names file, line and host. In tests/repo/test_deployment_neutral.py:111-119 the whole-repo test only asserts `found == []`. The other three tests (lines 122-141) call offending() and url_host_allowed() on strings: none of them calls tracked() or the per-file loop. So nothing checks that the scan reaches a real tracked file, that read errors don't skip files without anyone noticing, or that a hit comes out as `<path>:<line>: <host>`. I searched tests/ and harness/, and nothing else uses tracked() or offending(). Both mutants survive, so the finding holds as an unproven gap. The fix stays inside the current specs: factor the per-file scan into a function over a list of paths, plant a company host in a temp file and assert the exact `relpath:line: host` message, and assert that tracked() contains a known file such as AGENTS.md. None of the three patterns fits this gap.

claim: Every host under `.internal` or `.localhost` passes, so a deployment's internal hostname that carries its company name (for example erp.<company>.internal) or its realm can be committed, though AGENTS.md forbids hostnames and company names of a deployment.
evidence: PRIVATE = ('localhost', 'internal'), and url_host_allowed returns True for any _under(host, RESERVED + PRIVATE). offending() returned [] for `http://erp.<company>.internal` with a company label in it. The spec's text allows 'an address that isn't public', but the project rule in AGENTS.md lists hostnames and company names as deployment-specific, whether the name resolves publicly or not.
proposal: Test: assert that an `.internal` or `.localhost` host with more than one label below the private suffix, other than the names the e2e setup uses, is reported unless it is on an explicit list. Fix: allow only the private names the repository actually uses (put them on a list, like PUBLIC_HOSTS), not the whole suffix.

verdict.reproduction: I wrote a throwaway script under the scratchpad (repro_internal.py) that imports offending() from tests/repo/test_deployment_neutral.py and runs it on "http://erp.somecompany.internal" and "http://kc.somecompany.localhost/realms/x". It returned [], so the check does let these through. That is the behaviour the spec intends, so it is not a broken promise.
verdict.reason: Refuted because the specs say this behaviour is intended. The rule in AGENTS.md is put into practice by REQ-002-PRS-NF014 (docs/specs/req-002-service.md:298). That requirement lists "an address that isn't public" as an allowed kind of host, next to reserved example names and the public hosts on the list. The check at tests/repo/test_deployment_neutral.py:45-49 and :80-84 does exactly that: it allows the whole `internal` and `localhost` suffixes, and its comment calls `internal` the private-use domain "which no public site can have". The Definition of Done test test_examples_placeholders_and_addresses_that_arent_public_pass (:128-135) says on purpose that http://erp.internal:8000 passes, and private IPs such as 10.0.0.5 pass by the same rule. No check of host shapes can tell a company label under a private suffix from any other label: the same holds for private IPs and single-label hosts, which the spec allows too. Narrowing the allowance to a fixed list of private names, as the finding proposes, would change what REQ-002-PRS-NF014 says. That makes it a spec change, not a breach of the current contract. SECURITY.md and docs/backlog/backlog.md say nothing either way.

claim: With --push, the gate reuses the checks of an earlier passing record at the same commit even when that record was written before the secret scan existed. Such a branch is pushed to the public repository without ever being scanned.
evidence: main() loads the run's gates.jsonl (gate.py:470-472) and, with --push, takes `earlier = passed_earlier(records, branch, commit)` instead of running `_checks` (gate.py:503-508). passed_earlier (gate.py:181-188) only looks at branch, commit and passed:true. It never checks that the record's checks include "secrets", and `passed = all(checks.values())` holds for a check set that has no "secrets" key. Committed records like this exist now: harness/runs/2026-11-12-tests-2/gates.jsonl has 7 passed, unpushed records, 2026-11-14-tests and 2026-11-14-tests-2 have 2 each, and none of them contains "secrets". Steps: one of those branches still points at its recorded commit; the operator follows harness/README.md step 8 (gate without --push, then with it) and runs `gate.py harness/runs/2026-11-12-tests-2 <branch> --push`, so that branch is pushed with no gitleaks run. The same happens with a record written by hand. The test test_a_branch_that_passed_at_its_commit_is_pushed_without_a_second_run (tests/repo/test_harness.py:1270) even asserts that a check set without "secrets" ({ruff, tests}) gets reused.
proposal: Test: passed_earlier given a passing record whose checks lack "secrets" (or lack any key of CHECKS) returns None. Fix: return the earlier checks only if their keys equal {"secrets", *CHECKS}; otherwise run _checks again.

verdict.reason: The finding describes the code correctly but I could not reproduce a breach. passed_earlier (harness/gate.py:180-187) checks only branch, commit and passed, and only the branch's last record (mine[-1]) counts. Every record _checks writes now has a "secrets" key (gate.py:399), and secrets=false fails all(). So the gap only matters for a record written before baab778 (2026-11-15). I went through the committed runs it names (harness/runs/2026-11-12-tests-2, 2026-11-14-tests, 2026-11-14-tests-2) and kept the last record per branch. In every case that record passed and has pushed:true. The "unpushed" passed records the finding counts were each followed by a later record for the same branch, either at the same commit and pushed (2026-11-14-*) or at a new commit and pushed (2026-11-12-tests-2). So a --push that reuses a record can only push again a commit that was already pushed to the public remote. Nothing new reaches Git without a scan. No auto/ branches exist locally or under origin in this clone either (git for-each-ref shows none), so none still points at a recorded commit. The README's step 8 order (gate without --push first, then with it) writes a fresh record that includes the secret scan, and that fresh record is the one --push reuses. A gates.jsonl record written by hand comes from the operator, who could push by hand anyway, so it is outside the pipeline's gate. Missing secrets keys can be tightened, but on its own it breaks no promise. At most a later survey could report it as unproven/hardening: test_a_branch_that_passed_at_its_commit_is_pushed_without_a_second_run (tests/repo/test_harness.py:1270) uses a check set without "secrets", and no test requires one.

claim: The gate's secret scan reads `git log -p` without --text, so a secret inside a file that git treats as binary is never shown to gitleaks. The file is still pushed to the public repository.
evidence: patch() (gate.py:308-311) runs `git log -p --no-color --no-ext-diff fork..commit`. For a file containing a NUL byte, git prints only `Binary files /dev/null and b/<file> differ`. I checked this in a scratch repo: a file holding a NUL byte plus a marked line produced 0 matches for the marker in that output. The gate's path rules allow any new file under tests/ (ALLOWED, gate.py:49), and nothing refuses binary content. Steps: a fix agent's commit adds tests/fixtures/x.bin with a NUL byte followed by a key line; leaks() feeds the patch to gitleaks `stdin`, which finds nothing; `checks["secrets"]` is True; with --push the branch is pushed. The reviewer's `git show` also displays only `Binary files ... differ`. record.py is not affected: it scans the result text directly.
proposal: Test: a branch whose commit adds a file containing a NUL byte and 'LEAKED' gives gate.leaks(..., FAKE_SCANNER) is True. Fix: add --text (and -c core.attributesFile=/dev/null or --no-textconv) to the log in patch(), or refuse binary files in problems().

verdict.reproduction: I wrote a throwaway pytest at /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ubuntu-dev-enterich/0431a6bc-d8e6-4381-9c7d-b9072faa4363/scratchpad/bin/test_binleak.py that imports harness/gate.py and uses the same fake scanner as tests/repo/test_harness.py:2283 (exit 1 when 'LEAKED' is on stdin). It makes a scratch repo with a commit on main, then an auto/x branch whose `test:` commit adds tests/x.bin: a NUL byte, a newline, then a key line with the marker. Ran with `uv run pytest -s`; it passed. gate.patch() printed only "Binary files /dev/null and b/tests/x.bin differ" with no marker, gate.leaks(repo, fork, 'HEAD', FAKE) returned False, and `git show HEAD:tests/x.bin` still has the marker in the commit that would be pushed. No real secret was used; the planted value was the test's placeholder marker.
verdict.reason: harness/gate.py:308-311 patch() runs `git log -p --no-color --no-ext-diff` without --text, so git leaves out the content of any file it sees as binary. leaks() and secret() (gate.py:314-329) send only that text to gitleaks `stdin` (SCANNER, gate.py:101). _checks() (gate.py:~392) uses that result as checks["secrets"], and with --push a branch that passed is pushed to the public repository before CI's gitleaks runs on a PR. ALLOWED (gate.py:49) allows any new file under tests/, and gate.py has no binary refusal (grep finds no 'binary' or '--text'). The promise is AGENTS.md's "Secrets never in Git" (promises.jsonl line 12), and the gate's docstring says it does a secret scan of a branch's commits for that reason. Not out of scope: SECURITY.md's scope covers secrets appearing "anywhere else outside Enterich", and nothing on its out-of-scope list covers this. docs/backlog/backlog.md doesn't list it. REQ-002-URS-NF006 covers runtime logs and results and says nothing for or against this. The existing tests (tests/repo/test_harness.py:2286-2318) only use text files. The fix stays within the specs and ADRs: a test in tests/repo/test_harness.py next to the gate's secret-scan tests (a NUL-byte file holding the marker must give leaks() True), plus --text and --no-textconv in patch() in harness/gate.py. harness/ is on the pipeline's FORBIDDEN list, so the operator applies the code change, but no spec or ADR has to change. None of the three patterns fits.

claim: No test would notice if the secret scan were taken out of the gate's checks: no test calls _checks or main, so dropping the `"secrets": not leaks(...)` entry passes the whole suite.
evidence: _checks starts with `results = {"secrets": not leaks(ROOT, fork, commit)}` (gate.py:399). The scan tests in tests/repo/test_harness.py:2279-2325 call only gate.patch and gate.leaks directly, plus constant checks on SCANNER and SCANNER_IMAGE_DIR. A grep for `_checks` and `gate.main` in tests/ finds nothing. If line 399 became `results = {}` or `leaks(...)` were inverted, every test would still pass, and every branch would be pushed unscanned. The same goes for the bundle, which also goes through _checks (gate.py:555).
proposal: A test that runs _checks (with CHECKS and the scanner patched to fakes, the scanner flagging 'LEAKED') on a branch whose commit holds 'LEAKED' and asserts checks["secrets"] is False and the branch counts as not passed; or a main()-level test with --push asserting such a branch is not pushed.

verdict.reproduction: I copied HEAD into the scratchpad (scratchpad/copy) and changed harness/gate.py:399 from `{"secrets": not leaks(ROOT, fork, commit)}` to `{}`. Then I ran `uv run pytest tests/repo/test_harness.py`: 244 passed. With the secret scan gone from the gate's checks, no test failed.
verdict.reason: The finding holds as an unproven gap. harness/gate.py:399 is the only place the secret scan feeds into a branch's pass or fail, through `_checks`. `_checks` is called from `main` (gate.py:508) and from `_bundled` (gate.py:555). A grep of tests/, including e2e and integration, finds no test that calls `_checks`, `main` or `_bundled`. Gate tests live only in tests/repo/test_harness.py and call the helpers directly: `leaks`, `patch`, `bundle`, `problems`, `pushed`, `branch_state` and others. The mutation run above backs this up. The place does keep the promise: the gate pushes auto/ branches to the remote, and a branch that went out unscanned would put a secret into Git before CI's gitleaks runs on the pull request. SECURITY.md's scope doesn't exclude this, the backlog doesn't list it, and the specs and ADR-008 don't say the behaviour is intended. It can be closed within the current docs. The fix is a test in tests/repo/test_harness.py, where the gate tests are now. It would run `_checks` with CHECKS emptied and the scanner patched to flag a planted marker, then assert that checks["secrets"] is False and the branch doesn't pass (or that `main` with push doesn't push it). None of the three listed patterns fits.

claim: secret() fails closed (any non-zero exit of the scanner counts as a finding), but no test would notice if this were weakened to `returncode == 1`. A scanner that can't run, such as docker exiting 125 or 127 or a missing image, would then pass every branch and every record.
evidence: secret() returns `done.returncode != 0` (gate.py:314-324). gate.leaks and record.main both go through it. FAKE_SCANNER (tests/repo/test_harness.py:2283) only ever exits 0 or 1, so the mutant `== 1` survives all of the tests at 2286-2318 and 1484-1497. In real use, if the docker daemon stops after build_scanner or the image tag is removed, `docker run` exits 125 or 127: under the mutant, the gate records secrets:true and pushes, and record.py writes results unscanned.
proposal: A test with a scanner that exits 2 (e.g. [sys.executable, '-c', 'import sys; sys.exit(2)']) asserting gate.secret(...) is True and record.main(..., that scanner) == 1 writes nothing.

verdict.reproduction: I copied HEAD into the scratchpad with git archive and changed harness/gate.py:324 to `return done.returncode == 1`. Running `uv run pytest tests/repo tests/unit` on that copy gave 649 passed and 2 failed. Both failures (test_deployment_neutral's host check and the inventory-since-a-commit test) need a git checkout, which the archive copy doesn't have; neither is about the scan. A probe that calls gate.secret('x', ..., [python, -c, 'sys.exit(125)']) printed False on the mutant (the scan fails silently and counts as clean) and True on the real code.
verdict.reason: harness/gate.py:314-324 secret() counts any non-zero exit as a finding. gate.py:399 (secrets result for the push) goes through it via leaks() at gate.py:327, and so does record.main at harness/record.py:117. The only scanner fake in the tests is FAKE_SCANNER at tests/repo/test_harness.py:2283, and it exits only 0 or 1 (sys.exit of a bool). I searched all of tests/, tests/e2e included: no test uses a scanner that exits any other way. The only other scanner test (2321-2325) checks the SCANNER arguments. So the `== 1` mutant survives every test. That matters for secrets-never-in-git (AGENTS.md; REQ-002-URS-NF006): a docker run that exits 125 or 127 would let the gate push unscanned and let record.py write results unscanned. The fix is a test in tests/repo/test_harness.py with a scanner that exits 2: gate.secret/leaks must return True, and record.main must return 1 and write nothing. That stays within the current specs and ADRs. None of the three patterns fits, since this is about a subprocess's exit code.
